limitations: Source correspondence only; clinical classifications are not independently certified. All article components read, but phenotype specificity and several reported absences remain unresolved.

patient_identity.statement: Patient1 is the female liveborn subject in the clinical narrative and Figure2 pedigree, distinct from four fetuses in a thirdfamily; packet identity and sex correspond.

genotype.statement: Homozygous c.432G>C, GRCh38chr2:186625496G>C and predicted p.Trp144Cys match. RNA demonstrates novel splice-acceptor gain and p.Ala137AsnfsTer1; recombinant Trp144Cys retains function, so a simple missense loss-of-function interpretation would be incomplete.
limitations: Source uses NM_002210.4 versus packet .5; genomic coordinates/ref/alt and protein change match exactly. No independent transcript remapping.

segregation.statement: Both parents are heterozygous in the corresponding pedigree; the proband is homozygous. Miscarried fetuses have unknown genotypes and are not assigned causality.

phase.statement: Biallelic homozygosity with heterozygous parents supports recessive inheritance; no separate two-variant phase ambiguity.

causal_confidence.statement: The paper attributes immune/neurodevelopmental/colitis disease to biallelic ITGAV deficiency with segregation,RNA/protein and TGF-beta pathway evidence; this supports source causal attribution without independently validating PATHOGENIC/SOLVED labels.
limitations: Research functional findings do not establish independent clinical truth or a treatment recommendation.

phenotype_completeness.statement: Both packets encode elevated IgE as monoclonal without evidence of clonality. Several negatives are not explicitly documented; infantile seizures agree, but congenital-versus-later microcephaly and excluded IUGR remain unresolved.
limitations: No absence inferred from silence or a narrower diagnosis; all70phenotypes individually assessed below.
